Why DeSoto businesses miss calls

DeSoto sits in the Best Southwest area, south of Dallas, close to I-35E and major distribution routes. Transportation and utilities employ over 10% of workers, and education and health care about 24%. Many residents commute into Dallas or work shifts at warehouses, so calls often come early or late. Small professional offices and home service firms here cannot always keep a person by the phone at those times.

Which DeSoto businesses benefit most?

  • Medical offices: Commuters can book when they get home.
  • Law firms: New clients can reach intake outside office hours.
  • HVAC and contractors: Capture jobs while your crew is out.

Can you keep your DeSoto phone number?

Yes. DeSoto callers will usually see the 214, 469, 972 and 945 area codes, and you can keep the number customers already know. Everything is set up remotely, so you do not need new equipment or a visit to an office.

What to check before you go live

  1. Test real calls: ask awkward questions, not only easy ones, and listen to how it handles them.
  2. Set the rules: decide which calls transfer to a person and which become messages.
  3. Plan your minutes: estimate your busiest month, not an average one.
  4. Tell callers what you need to: Texas is generally treated as a one-party consent state for recording calls, but rules differ for callers in other states, so check with your advisor if you record calls.
